children: is beginning wider deliveries of its Semi electric trucks this week, executives said at an event late Thursday at its plant in Sparks, Nevada, nearly nine years after CEO Elon Musk unveiled the vehicle. Tesla shares were up 1.01% in premarket.

The company didn't disclose pricing or production volume plans, though it reiterated its target of building 50,000 Semis a year in Nevada. Customers including PepsiCo (PEP), DHL and US Foods (USFD) appeared on stage. Tesla said the long-range version can travel 500 miles on a single charge when loaded, while a standard version offers 325 miles. Musk, who didn't attend, said in a recorded message that "the waiting list is already pretty significant."

The Semi has been a long time coming. Production was originally expected in 2019, and limited deliveries to PepsiCo began in late 2022, but delays, rising competition and a reversal in U.S. EV policy have raised concerns about demand. Orders have picked up recently. A coalition of large shippers including Microsoft (MSFT) and PepsiCo placed an order for 2,500 Semis this week, according to clean transportation nonprofit Catalyst Mobility. Last month, Swedish freight technology company Einride added 500 Semis to its fleet.

title: Tesla Starts Semi Deliveries Nearly Nine Years After Unveiling
